name: NORD Patient Assistance Programs
description: NORD Patient Assistance Programs help individuals living with rare diseases obtain life-saving or life-sustaining medications they could not otherwise afford. NORD administers over 60 individual patient assistance programs funded by pharmaceutical manufacturers and private donors. Programs cover medication costs, insurance co-pays, diagnostic testing, and travel expenses for treatment. NORD serves patients regardless of immigration status and provides multilingual support for non-English speakers navigating the U.S. healthcare system.
eligibility: Individuals diagnosed with a qualifying rare disease who meet financial need criteria. Open to all U.S. residents regardless of immigration status. Income thresholds vary by program.
amount: Varies by program — covers medication, co-pays, diagnostics, and travel costs
applicationProcess: Apply online through NORD's website or call the NORD helpline. A healthcare provider must confirm the rare disease diagnosis. Financial documentation may be required depending on the specific program.
documentsRequired: Diagnosis confirmation from a physician, proof of income or financial hardship, insurance information (if applicable), prescription details

name: PCRF Treatment Abroad Program
description: The PCRF Treatment Abroad Program arranges free medical care for sick and injured children from the Middle East at hospitals in the United States, Europe, and Asia. Since 1992, PCRF has sent over 2,000 children for life-saving surgeries, cancer treatment, cardiac care, and other specialized procedures not available in their home countries. PCRF covers all costs including medical treatment, travel, accommodation, and post-operative follow-up care. The program works with partner hospitals worldwide and provides visa sponsorship and family support throughout the treatment process.
eligibility: Children from the Middle East (primarily Palestine, Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Iraq) who require specialized medical treatment not available in their home country. No financial requirements — all costs are covered by PCRF.
amount: Full coverage — medical treatment, travel, accommodation, and follow-up care
applicationProcess: Referral from a local physician or hospital documenting the child's condition and the need for treatment abroad. PCRF medical team reviews cases and matches children with appropriate hospitals. Visa sponsorship and travel arrangements are handled by PCRF.
geographicScope: International — treatment provided in the USA, Europe, and Asia; patients from the Middle East
documentsRequired: Medical records and diagnosis from local physician, passport or travel documents for the child and accompanying parent, referral letter from local hospital
targetDiagnosis: Complex pediatric conditions including cancer, cardiac defects, orthopedic conditions, burns, and other conditions requiring specialized surgical or medical intervention

name: SickKids International Patient Program (IPP)
organization: The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), Toronto
description: The SickKids International Patient Program provides access to world-class specialized pediatric care for children living outside of Canada who cannot receive the treatment they need in their home country or region. SickKids is one of the world's leading pediatric hospitals, offering expertise in complex surgeries, rare diseases, cancer treatment, and advanced diagnostics. The IPP team coordinates all aspects of international patient care including medical consultations, visa support letters, accommodation referrals, and interpreter services for families who do not speak English or French.
eligibility: Children up to 17 years of age from outside Canada who require specialized pediatric care not available in their home region. Treatment must be completed before the patient's 18th birthday. Patients or their sponsors are responsible for costs unless a sponsoring organization covers them.
amount: Varies — costs depend on treatment; charitable sponsorship and humanitarian cases may be funded
applicationProcess: Submit a referral through the IPP online portal or contact the international patient coordinator. Medical records must be provided for review by SickKids specialists. If accepted, the IPP team assists with logistics, visa letters, and accommodation.
geographicScope: Canada (Toronto) — accepts patients from all countries worldwide
documentsRequired: Complete medical records, diagnostic imaging, physician referral letter, passport, proof of financial responsibility or sponsorship letter
targetDiagnosis: Complex pediatric conditions including rare diseases, childhood cancers, congenital heart defects, neurological disorders, and conditions requiring advanced surgical intervention

name: NIH Clinical Center International Patient Program (B-2 Visa)
organization: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical Center
description: The NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland, is the world's largest hospital dedicated to clinical research. International patients can participate in NIH clinical trials at no cost — all medical care, tests, and procedures related to the research protocol are provided free of charge. The NIH supports international participants by providing B-2 visa sponsorship letters, covering travel costs in some protocols, and offering interpreter services. This is a unique opportunity for patients with rare, complex, or treatment-resistant conditions to access cutting-edge experimental therapies while contributing to medical research.
eligibility: International patients who meet the specific eligibility criteria for an active NIH clinical trial. No insurance or payment is required — all research-related care is free. Participants must qualify medically for the study protocol.
amount: Free — all research-related medical care, tests, and procedures at no cost to the patient
applicationProcess: Search active clinical trials on ClinicalTrials.gov or the NIH Clinical Center website. Contact the study team directly to determine eligibility. If eligible, the NIH provides a B-2 visa sponsorship letter for international patients. The study team coordinates all logistics.
geographicScope: United States (Bethesda, Maryland) — open to patients from all countries worldwide
documentsRequired: Medical records relevant to the clinical trial, passport, B-2 visa application (NIH provides sponsorship letter), signed informed consent for the research protocol
targetDiagnosis: Varies by clinical trial — includes rare diseases, cancer, autoimmune disorders, genetic conditions, infectious diseases, and other conditions under active research
ageRange: Varies by protocol — many trials accept adults and children

name: Global Genes RARE Patient Impact Grants
description: Global Genes RARE Patient Impact Grants provide direct financial assistance to individuals and families affected by rare diseases worldwide. Grants help cover costs related to medical treatment, travel for specialist appointments, adaptive equipment, genetic testing, and other expenses not covered by insurance. Global Genes is one of the leading rare disease advocacy organizations globally, supporting patients across borders and connecting them with resources, clinical trials, and support communities. The grant program is open to applicants internationally and does not require U.S. citizenship.
eligibility: Individuals or families affected by a diagnosed rare disease. Open to applicants worldwide. Financial need must be demonstrated. The rare disease diagnosis must be confirmed by a medical professional.
applicationProcess: Apply online during open grant cycles through the Global Genes website. Applications require a personal statement, physician confirmation of rare disease diagnosis, description of intended use of funds, and financial need documentation.
geographicScope: International — open to rare disease patients worldwide
documentsRequired: Physician letter confirming rare disease diagnosis, personal statement describing impact and intended use of funds, proof of financial need
targetDiagnosis: Any diagnosed rare disease (there are approximately 7,000 known rare diseases)

name: Refugee Health Promotion (RHP) Program
organization: Administration for Children and Families (ACF), Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)
description: The Refugee Health Promotion (RHP) Program funds community-based organizations to deliver direct health services that promote the health and well-being of newly arrived refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. RHP-funded services include health education, mental health support, chronic disease management, health system navigation, preventive care coordination, and culturally and linguistically appropriate health outreach. The program addresses health disparities among refugee communities and helps newcomers access and navigate the U.S. healthcare system during their critical first years of resettlement.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, victims of trafficking, and other ORR-eligible populations in the United States. Services are provided through funded community organizations at no cost to the individual.
amount: Free services — funded through federal grants to community organizations
applicationProcess: Services are available through ORR-funded community organizations. Contact your local resettlement agency or refugee health program to access services. No individual application required — eligibility is based on ORR-eligible immigration status.
geographicScope: United States — Nationwide through funded community organizations
documentsRequired: Proof of ORR-eligible immigration status (I-94, refugee/asylee documentation)
targetDiagnosis: General health promotion — covers mental health, chronic disease, preventive care, and health education

name: Cancer Research UK Clinical Trials for International Patients
description: Cancer Research UK funds and coordinates hundreds of clinical trials across the United Kingdom that are open to international patients. Patients from outside the UK can participate in cancer clinical trials, gaining access to experimental treatments, immunotherapies, and targeted therapies not yet widely available. While patients generally need to cover their own travel and accommodation costs, all trial-related medical treatment is provided free through the NHS. Cancer Research UK provides guidance on visa requirements, trial eligibility, and how to arrange referrals from overseas oncologists to UK trial centers.
eligibility: International cancer patients who meet the specific medical eligibility criteria for an active UK clinical trial. Patients must be able to travel to the UK for treatment visits. A referral from the patient's current oncologist is typically required.
amount: Free trial-related treatment through the NHS; travel and accommodation costs are the patient's responsibility
applicationProcess: Search for suitable trials on the Cancer Research UK website or ClinicalTrials.gov. Contact the trial team to confirm eligibility. Arrange a referral from your current oncologist. The trial center can provide letters to support visa applications.
geographicScope: United Kingdom — trial centers across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland; open to patients from any country
documentsRequired: Complete oncology medical records, referral letter from current oncologist, diagnostic pathology reports, passport and UK visa (trial center provides support letter)
targetDiagnosis: All cancer types — including breast, lung, colorectal, blood cancers, brain tumors, rare cancers, and pediatric cancers
ageRange: Varies by trial — many accept adults 18+; some pediatric trials available
